title: Redwood discovery with AstraQuant - cost & economics
summary: Discovery focused on Redwood pricing levers: per-token hosted pricing, reserved/dedicated discounts, batching and prefix/KV caching impacts on unit cost. AstraQuant has strict monthly budget targets and wants an initial pilot to validate 1M request throughput and unit economics. Next steps: pricing sheet, security docs, schedule pilot benchmark.
next_steps: Samir to send hosted vs dedicated pricing sheet and cost model (by 2026-12-24)
Jules to share recommended batching/caching config and quantization options (by 2026-12-27)
AstraQuant to provide sample traffic profile and 7-day traces for benchmark (by 2026-12-29)
Schedule 2-hour pilot kickoff / benchmark session week of 2027-01-04
action_items: Samir Patel: Send hosted vs dedicated pricing sheet and example cost calc (due 2026-12-24)
Jules Martin: Share batching/caching config + suggested quantization profile (due 2026-12-27)
Maya Chen: Provide representative traffic traces and a 7-day sample dataset (due 2026-12-29)
Nora White: Confirm procurement timeline and PO process (due 2027-01-07)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-22 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m | Recorder: Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Martin (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (AstraQuant, Head of ML), Liam Ortiz (AstraQuant, Platform Lead), Nora White (AstraQuant, Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Focus on unit economics and trade-offs between hosted and dedicated/private. Discussed per-token examples, batching and KV caching levers, committed capacity discounts, and an initial pilot to benchmark real costs.

00:00 Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm samir from redwood, nice to meet you all, um quick roll call then we'll jump in.
00:07 Maya: hey samir, maya here, hi liam, nora, thanks.
00:12 Liam: yep, liam on the infra side.
00:15 Nora: nora from procurement.
00:18 Samir: awesome. Jules i think you wanted to lead the cost part?
00:22 Jules: yeah i'll take the cost / performance section, i'll also show how batching and prefix caching moves the needle a lot. few disclaimers: numbers we'll discuss are ballpark until we run a benchmark with your traces.

02:05 Maya: to set context, we're building an automated summarization + Q&A layer on top of financial filings. average doc size ~2k tokens, we do chunking, typical request ends up 600-800 tokens total response+prompt. monthly active users around 25k, we expect a steady 1.5M requests per month at peak — ballpark.
02:28 Samir: okay good. quick qualification: is data residency or on-prem a hard requirement?
02:33 Maya: not initially. security is important — SOC2, audit logs, key mgmt — but we're open to hosted if the economics make sense.
02:39 Samir: great. also helpful to know target budget for LLM infra?
02:42 Liam: procurement target is 20k-30k per month for model spend initially — we can expand if unit economics are favorable.

04:10 Jules: great, so quick pass on pricing: our hosted API pricing is usage-based (per-token). for example for a mid-sized open model equivalency we'd estimate ~ $0.00045 per input token and $0.0018 per output token at list — again this is illustrative and varies by model. for customers that commit to Dedicated reserved capacity we offer effective per-token reductions via committed monthly vGPU hours and priority capacity — typically 30-45% off the hosted list depending on commit. private (on-prem/vpc) is licensed + infra so the unit economics depend on customer infra costs and utilization.
04:50 Maya: ok can you run that into our numbers — with 1.5M requests and 700 tokens average that's about 1.05B tokens/month? wait let me do the math.
04:58 Liam: 1.5M * 700 = 1.05 billion tokens yes.
05:05 Jules: correct. rough hosted cost estimate (list rates) — say 1.05B tokens * averaged blended $0.0012 per token (weighted input/output) = about $1.26M / month which obviously is way over your target.
05:18 Maya: yikes that's way too high, ok we need levers.

06:00 Jules: levers we typically look at: batching, prefix/KV caching, model selection and quantization. batching reduces compute wall clock per token by increasing throughput on GPU but can increase tail latency — for many of your queries that are async-ish we can batch aggressively. prefix caching (we call it KV cache/prefix cache) helps when prompts share common prefixes, e.g., standard instruction templates or prior context; that can cut token compute by 20-60% depending on reuse. quantization lets you run a smaller model variant at similar quality for certain workloads at much lower cost.
06:38 Samir: to put numbers, if you can get 5x effective cost reduction via batching + caching + model choice we can get to ~ $250k/mo on hosted which is still high but closer. with dedicated reserved capacity and 40% discount you'd be around $150k/mo. with an optimized private deployment and high utilization perhaps $90-120k but that assumes you can fully utilize reserved infra.
07:05 Maya: still above our 20-30k target — what about caching at the application layer — deduping requests?
07:12 Liam: we do a lot of dedupe — about 30% are repeat-ish queries within a session. plus we have precomputed embeddings for some flows.
07:20 Jules: great — that helps. also think about partial responses/collapsing: some flows don't need full 700 tokens; you can put a scoring layer to limit generation. those changes can reduce tokens/request by 30-60% depending on UX tradeoff.

09:00 Nora: from procurement POV, we need clear cost per 1M tokens and an estimate for month 1 pilot. can you provide a simple calc?
09:06 Samir: yes, we'll send a hosted vs dedicated vs private one-page calc with assumptions. example line: Hosted list — $0.0012 blended per token -> cost per 1M tokens = $1,200. Dedicated effective -> $700 per 1M tokens (example after commit). Private infra -> depends, e.g., self-host with P4-like fleet and 70% utilization might get to $450-600 per 1M tokens all-in.
09:40 Maya: that hosted $1,200 per 1M seems more manageable to reason about. if you can show scenario where our traffic after dedupe+cache drops to 150M tokens then cost at hosted list is $180k — still high but closer.

11:15 Jules: quick walk-through of how we measure the caching benefit: we instrument prefix share rate and we estimate effective token savings = prefix_reuse_fraction * prefix_token_count. so a 40% reuse on a 200-token prefix yields 80 tokens saved on average. we can run a quick sim if you give traces.
11:40 Liam: we can provide 7 days of traces — request/response token counts + hashes for dedupe.
11:45 Samir: perfect that's exactly what we need for a pilot.

13:00 Maya: curious about tail latency with aggressive batching — some of our users expect sub-400ms 90th pct for chat-ish flows. does batching break that?
13:10 Jules: it's a tradeoff — if you need strict sub-400ms SLO, batching is limited, but KV/prefix caching helps a lot because it reduces compute without adding queueing. there's also smart routing — low-latency tier for a fraction of traffic and a cost-optimized tier for background queries.
13:35 Samir: we can do split routing by user segment — e.g., 10% of requests go to low-latency dedicated pool, rest go to cost-optimized hosted pools. that brings blended cost down.

15:00 Nora: security questions — do you provide KMS/HSM integration and customer-managed keys in hosted?
15:06 Jules: yes we integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping, and we support VPC peering for private deployments. we'll share SOC2 + architecture docs.
15:15 Nora: please add that to the packet.

16:05 Maya: what's the typical discount curve for committed Dedicated? for example if we commit $50k/mo do we get 30%?
16:12 Samir: typical discounts scale with commit and term; $50k/mo commit could be in the 25-35% range depending on model mix and guarantee. bigger commits 40%+. we also offer burst windows for traffic spikes.
16:30 Liam: how does bursting work? if we have reserved 70% baseline but spike to 200%, how do we get capacity?
16:36 Jules: there's a configured burst capacity for Dedicated customers — you pay for baseline commit and additional usage billed at a blended overage rate; we can set soft caps and alarms.

18:00 Maya: can you run a sample calc live? i want to see hosted list vs reserved dedicated with dedupe/caching assumptions.
18:05 Samir: sure — quick hypothetical: baseline 1.05B tokens. assume dedupe + app optimizations reduce tokens 60% -> ~420M tokens. assume caching/prefix + batching = additional 50% compute reduction on those tokens effective -> equivalent charged tokens ~210M. hosted list at $1,200 per 1M => $252k/mo. dedicated 35% discount -> ~$164k/mo. with private and high utilization maybe ~$95k/mo.
18:45 Maya: ok that's still outside our initial budget but gives us levers.

20:10 Jules: for the pilot we typically recommend: 1) share traces 2) we run a 7-day benchmark against candidate models and configs (batching + cache) 3) produce a per-1M token cost and projected monthly bill under your actual traffic. Pilot is usually 2-3 weeks.
20:25 Maya: sounds good. timeline wise we need procurement signoff by mid january. if we start pilot early january that's tight but possible.

22:00 Samir: we'll put together an engagement doc and pricing scenarios today/tomorrow. expect a pricing sheet + security packet + pilot plan.

24:00 (ambient chatter, background typing)

25:30 Liam: one more technical question — you mentioned automated prefix caching: how persistent is the KV cache across replicas/scale events?
25:40 Jules: KV cache is sharded with TTLs and sticky affinity to keep hot prefixes local; on scale events we warm via async prefetch and a small miss rate is normal. caching is transparent to the app. occasionally transcription notes call it K-V cash, you might see that in logs.

28:00 Nora: procurement note: we'll need PO details and standard SLA language — can you include sample SLA for latency and uptime?
28:07 Samir: yes will include sample SLA and standard terms.

30:00 Maya: any known limitations on model choices in Dedicated? e.g., we want to run quantized variants and some of the bleeding-edge open models.
30:08 Jules: we support a wide catalog — we validate model performance and have recommended quantization profiles; there are a few experimental combos but we can test them in the pilot.

33:00 Maya: okay recap — our constraints: 20-30k target, likely can't reach that at current usage without major product changes; immediate ask is a pilot to quantify realistic cost after dedupe/cache/model changes.
33:12 Samir: recap from our side: 1) send hosted vs dedicated vs private cost sheet (samir) 2) share batching and quantization recommendations + config (jules) 3) receive traces and schedule a 2-hour kickoff to run pilot (all) 4) include SOC2/KMS docs and sample SLA (samir)
33:30 Nora: procurement will review pricing sheet first, then we can lock dates.

35:00 (brief pause)

36:20 Maya: one last question — do you have customers in regulated fintech who started on hosted and moved to dedicated? any case study?
36:28 Samir: yes we have a handful — we'll include a short case snippet (anonymized) about a fintech customer who reduced cost per 1M tokens from ~900 to ~350 after batching, caching, and reserved capacity.

38:00 Jules: ok i'll follow up on the technical checklist for the pilot: what artifacts we need, what metrics we'll report (tokens saved, effective tokens, p95 latency, cost per 1M).

40:00 Maya: great. thanks everyone.
40:05 Samir: thanks all, we'll follow up with the packet.
40:09 Meeting end.
